Unfinished Business

26 - 29 August

Book
Tickets

Would you rewrite a past decision that could change your future?

The year is 2100. No one really goes out anymore. Everything happens in the virtual world. 

A group of teenagers have been challenged to find disregarded objects from the past. What they discover changes how they see themselves and the choices they make. 

Unfinished Business is a show about choice and ownership. Why do we make the decisions we make? What would happen if we rewrote past choices? And really, are they ours to begin with?

Blending personal stories, imagined futures and live sound created on stage, Unfinished Business invites the audience on a journey through past choices, consequences and towards hope.

Company Three returns to New Diorama Theatre with Unfinished Business, co-created by the company and written and directed by Associate Director Mariana Aristizábal Pardo.

Post-Show Talk Back

Thursday 27 August, 8:30pm-9pm

Step into the world of Unfinished Business with our brilliant cast and Director Mariana Aristizábal Pardo. Discover the ideas and journey behind the show - and explore how co-creation and youth voice shapes a Company Three play.

Company

Company Three is a leading force for change for teenagers in our local community and around the world.

We are a theatre company led by the ideas of our 75 members aged 11-19. We make performances in which our members can express themselves and the change they want to make, for audiences of people who have the most influence over their lives.

Working in Islington, North London, we make transformative theatre through long-term collaboration between young people and professional artists. We recruit our members through deep-rooted relationships locally and share our practice globally to impact teenagers everywhere.

Our plays have been performed at the National Theatre, Battersea Arts Centre, the Royal Exchange Theatre, the Yard Theatre, the Park Theatre, New Diorama Theatre and on the BBC. Our short films have been screened at the British Film Institute. 

We share our practice locally, nationally and internationally. Our blueprints have been used by more than 500 groups in more than 30 countries to co-create work with young people. We have trained hundreds of artists through our training courses.

Our awards include the Best Micro Documentary Little Flix London Film Festival, Peter Brook Empty Space Award for Innovation, The Stage Award for Community Project of the Year, and Outstanding Drama Initiative at the Music and Drama Education Awards.

At Company Three we believe youth theatre can be a place of community, radical art and social change. Despite our global reach, we are fiercely local to and are proud to work with the young people of Islington about the issues which affect them most.

www.companythree.co.uk | @companythree

AMPLIFY

11 & 12 September

Book
Tickets

A bold new devised work from the alumni of Kestrel Theatre Company.

Created from scratch over a two-week process, AMPLIFY is a creative collaboration between playwright Molly Taylor (Young Vic, Almeida Theatre) and Kestrel’s alumni acting company.

Kestrel alumni are men the Kestrel team met when they were in prison or at risk of entering it. A significant part of Kestrel’s work is centred on supporting alumni to build sustainable creative careers on the outside, which includes developing original, devised, productions that centre the creative voices and artistry of the men involved.

‘Without this theatre company, I would still be incarcerated. They gave me a platform to express myself and, after my release, have continuously enabled me to climb the mountains in front of me’

Credits

Devised by a cast of Kestrel alumni in collaboration with playwright Molly Taylor.

Company

Kestrel Theatre is a transformative force within the UK criminal justice system, creating original pieces of theatre, film and live performance with people with lived experience of the prison system.

Founded in 1999, Kestrel works both within and beyond prison settings, working with participants to co-create original, professional-quality artistic work. Our projects include annual winter family shows within prisons, original documentary films, and productions for public-facing audiences. 

Kestrel’s notable public productions include Ignite (New Diorama, 2025), Youngers (New Diorama, 2022), Broken Dreams (Royal Court, 2017 & 2018), Blood and Water (Royal Court, 2016). Films include Saving Face (starring Sharon Duncan Brewster) and After Time.

www.kestreltheatrecompany.co.uk | @kestreltheatre

The First Year (of the Gaza Genocide in the Media)

22 September - 10 October 2026

Book
Tickets

These are the events as they were reported from October 7th 2023 to October 7th 2024.

The show you are about to watch has happened.

The show you are about to watch is happening.

The show you are about to watch is one you’ve been told could never happen again.

Award-winning international company BÉZNĂ Theatre presents a blistering multimedia investigation into the relationship between mainstream media, public opinion, and state crime. Created in collaboration with globally renowned researchers Shadow World Investigations and the International State Crime Initiative, and rooted in direct testimony from Palestinians in Gaza, The First Year (of the Gaza Genocide in the Media) is a wildly theatrical interrogation of the widening gulf between what we're told, what we witness, and what we choose to believe.

Featuring original music and an all-Palestinian and Palestinian heritage ensemble, this visually striking and visceral world premiere confronts the nature of truth in reporting, dismantling the machinery used to construct and distort public perception and illuminating the human cost behind journalistic choices.

BÉZNĂ Theatre exposes a performance staged by national broadcasters on October 7th 2023. The performance started long before that date. The performance started long before this show.

Previous Press for BÉZNǍ Theatre

★★★★★ ‘Powerful and hard-hitting [...] here's to more art questioning the status quo’ North West End

★★★★ ‘Raw humanity’ London Theatre Reviews

‘Theatre that burns’ Teatrul Azi (Theatre Today)

‘Powerful [...] a call to arms, a piece of activism and art’ The Guardian

But What Can I Do? Wraparound Programme

Inspired by the questions at the heart of The First Year (of the Gaza Genocide in the Media), But What Can I Do? is a hands-on programme bringing together artists, researchers, investigators, and community members to explore together state crime, media narratives, corruption, and collective action.

Shadow World Investigations Workshops

Led by Shadow World Investigations (SWI), these online workshops introduce tools and techniques used to investigate and track the global arms trade. Participants will explore how information is tracked and verified, learn about common tools and databases used in investigations, and discover how researchers build evidence using digital tools and networks. 

Artist Workshop: Monday 28th September, 6-8pm, online

Community Workshop: Monday 5th October, 6-8pm, online

 

International State Crime Initiative Workshops

Led by the International State Crime Initiative (ISCI), these workshops explore how state crime is defined, understood, and reported. Together, we'll examine the role of the media in shaping public narratives and consider best practice for engaging with the events of October 2023 - October 2024. 

Artist Workshop: Friday 2nd October, 4-6pm, New Diorama Theatre

Community Workshop: Friday 9th October, 4-6pm, New Diorama Theatre

 

Sign up for SWI and/or ISCI Artist Workshops

Sign up for SWI and/or ISCI Community Workshops

 

Producing Political Theatre Workshop

Run by BÉZNĂ Theatre's Claire Gilbert, this is a practical two hour session for theatre makers, looking at navigating the complexity of producing political theatre, paying particular attention to funding, differing external pressures and process.

Tuesday 6th October 4-6pm, New Diorama Theatre

Sign up for Producing Political Theatre Workshop

 

Media Ethics: A Post-Show Q+A

Join Dr Mike Berry (Cardiff University School of Journalism, Media, and Cultural Studies) in conversation with The First Year team as they explore the ethics of journalism, testimony and media coverage that sit at the heart of the production.

What happens when journalistic practices of impartiality, verification and editorial judgement come into contact with public policy and changing legal frameworks?

Drawing on Mike’s report into broadcasting bias, this Q&A will examine how journalists, researchers and artists work with data — and the ethical questions that arise when reality is necessarily selected, filtered and framed through the processes of journalism, research and theatre. 

Thursday 1st October, post-show

BÉZNĂ Theatre is an award-winning British-Romanian theatre collective that creates radical, visually striking theatre, encourages grassroots activism and exposes and resists institutionalised and normalised violences. Formed in Lincolnshire in 2013 and working on the frontline of Romanian and British political theatre and activism ever since, BÉZNĂ reclaims the theatre as an intersectional space of resistance, igniting dissent and empowering communities to speak back.

STUFFED

13 - 24 October 2026

Book
Tickets

This is about food banks. This is not about food.

This is about the bad stuff. This is an emergency. This is a clowning show.

Multi-award-winners Ugly Bucket present a blazing inferno of physicality, electronica, and uncompromising personal testimony from the frontlines of the UK’s food banks. As phones ring, guts spill, and sparks ignite faster than they can be extinguished, five clowns search for hope and community in the face of helplessness. Created in association with Liverpool’s Unity Theatre, STUFFED is a roaring call to action amidst the wreckage of a desecrated system.

More than a show, STUFFED is an invitation to gather — an evening of food, electrifying theatre, and empowering discussion illuminating the dark corners and exploring the power of collective action. All performances are captioned and accompanied by a free community meal and local food donation drive.

Winner of The Stage Fringe Five

Press

★★★★★ ‘As enraging as it is brilliant. A tour-de-force performance that deserves the nation’s attention.’ Opening Nights 

★★★★★ ‘You could hear a pin drop in the furthest corner of the room.’ North West End

★★★★★ 'Exhilarating' Theatre Weekly

★★★★ 'A remarkable piece of theatre' Financial Times

★★★★ 'A new direction [...] absolutely furious' The Stage

'Horrifically funny [...] a shining example of a young company, genuinely finding the form to match a show about a national emergency.' Lyn Gardner

The Good Stuff Wraparound Programme

STUFFED is more than a show.

Every performance is accompanied by The Good Stuff: a programme of shared meals, practical action, and conversations that continue long after the house lights come up. 

Designed to bring audiences together around the realities of food poverty, it’s an invitation not just to watch, but to take part. And there’s more than enough to go around.

Free Pre-Show Community Meal

6:30pm, New Diorama Theatre

Before every performance, audiences are invited to share a free communal meal together. Whether you're arriving with friends or flying solo, it's a chance to pull up a chair, meet the people around you, and start the evening in good company.

Because the thing about food is: it gives you time.

The Good Stuff Post-Show Gathering

8:45pm, New Diorama Theatre

The conversation doesn't end when the show does.

After each performance, local organisations tackling food poverty and community need will join us for a practical, action-focused conversation. Find out what's already happening in the area, hear from people doing the work, and discover how your own time, skills, resources, or networks could make a difference.

No expertise required. Get involved.

Food Donation Drive

From your donation, to on-stage prop, to community resource.

Audience members are invited to donate food and essential toiletries, which will become part of the show before being redistributed to local food banks and community organisations.

Donation requests will be tailored to the needs of our local partners, with more information shared ahead of your visit.

Created and originally co-produced in association with Unity Theatre. The 2026 tour and wraparound programme is supported by New Diorama Theatre, Arts Council England, National Lottery Community Fund, and Cockayne Grants for the Arts, a Donor Advised Fund, held at The Prism Charitable Trust.

Company

Described as 'one of the UK's most exciting young companies' (New Diorama) and named one of The Stage Fringe Five Breakthrough Theatre Makers Of The Future (2024) - Ugly Bucket are a Liverpool based national touring company that create hilarious gut-punching shows combining clown with physicality, original electronic music and personal testimony. They are often outrageous, audacious and always honest, working closely with communities to respond to current themes in a bold way.

Beyond their shows, they champion the clowning practice as a dynamic tool for community bonding, self exploration and social change. They believe when people are laughing they are listening, and use humour as a catalyst for deeper connections. They share their practice through workshops nationally and internationally, and host a yearly clowning retreat at Bidston Observatory Artistic Research Centre.

www.uglybuckettheatre.co.uk | @uglybuckettheatre

Orlando: A Pornobiography

10 November - 12 December 2026

Book
Tickets

SISSY: Advice to the young. It’s only dress-up. Don’t let it ruin your life.

Three boys, hunting on palace grounds, spot a girl. Two strangers skate together on the frozen River Thames. A young man and a married crossdresser meet for a playdate. Centuries pass, and Orlando has just bought a plane ticket to Neukölln, Berlin.

Part pornographic bildungsroman, part frosted fever dream, Orlando: A Pornobiography is a restless transmission across time. Gliding between the surreal and the hyperreal, this unruly epic sees the 16th Century ring a phone sex hotline to find the 21st Century on the other end of the line, asking for a body capable of surviving its own desire.

Across erotic entanglements, historical ruptures, and queer intrusions, an ensemble of transfemme performers tear through Virginia Woolf’s Orlando in this brazen anti-adaptation, a world premiere from award-winning duo piss / CARNATION.

Company

piss / CARNATION make fervent and interdisciplinary theatre work about transfemininity. They combine brutality with tenderness, abjection with glamour and experimental forms with uncompromising honesty. Their work has been called “brazen” (⭑⭑⭑⭑ Guardian), “gloriously extreme” (⭑⭑⭑⭑ The Stage) and “the future of theatre” (⭑⭑⭑⭑⭑ Broadway World). Their work includes 52 Monologues for Young Transsexuals and Ugly Sisters, both of which were received to acclaim.

Programmes for 11-30’s in music, media, performing arts and freelancer and entrepreneurship skills.

Autumn Youth Programme

Creativity belongs to everyone! This autumn, dive into our new season of music, media, performing arts and business programmes for 11-30s. 

From theatre to film funding to DJing, VR and game design, find your creative passion with expert tutors in a world-class space. This is your playground!

As a youth charity, we believe money shouldn’t stop anyone from getting creative. That’s why all our programmes are under £25. Plus, financial support is available for those who need it.

Youth Programme

We don't just put on unforgettable gigs and performances. Every ticket purchased helps us empower young people with affordable opportunities for ages 11-30 in music, media, performing arts and professional development.

Music
Whether you want to make music or get to know the industry, this is the place to start. 
Media
Workshops in content creation, radio, broadcasting, film-making and more.
Performing Arts
Spoken word, theatre, circus skills, dance, performance and backstage opportunities. 
Self Made
Our Self Made programme covers professional development for creative freelancers and entrepreneurs.

Home Venue hire Fashion Events

Fashion Show & Event Venue Hire London

Make a statement at the Roundhouse

We’ve hosted some of the biggest names in fashion, including Chanel, Tommy Hilfiger, Bulgari and Lacoste.

The versatility of the Roundhouse knows no end; whether you’re wanting to create the longest catwalk London Fashion Week has ever seen, or you simply want London’s most iconic venue to show off next season’s fashion trends – our team can make it happen in our space.

Our Main Space can seat up to 850 guests to watch the show, and our balcony offers an additional 503 seats with an overhead view. We have branding opportunities all over the space, including huge poster spots on the exterior of the building, which you can make full use of. You can go loud and proud and make your mark here at the Roundhouse!

We also have adequate space inside for a press wall, dressing rooms and production offices. So, get in touch today and make the Roundhouse your next catwalk.

            Bron’s life is complete, utter chaos.
        </section>
    
    

    
        <section class="content--text">
             <p>Three kids – an emotional tweenager, a four-year old stalker and the middle one. Just when things couldn’t get any harder, she bought a puppy. A million plates in the air, even more smashed on the ground around her feet. Bron wears the battle scars of an ex high-school teacher and is still reeling from the initial shock of motherhood 12 years ago. Tackling juggle-parenting, teaching, career change and flailing mental health, if you’ve ever thought ‘if one thing goes wrong, we’re all dead meat’ this is the show for you.</p>
<p>VicScreen Greenlight Award Winner and total sold-out run, Melbourne International Comedy Festival 2026.</p>

About 12 Days

This Christmas, five children are chosen for an extraordinary journey to discover the true meaning of love. Travelling through a divided world, they uncover empathy, trust, courage and belonging - learning that love grows when we come together. 

12 Days is a joyful, heart-warming festive adventure for all ages, brought to life in a spectacular Chickenshed production with a large, diverse cast - not to be missed!

Age Recommendation

12 Days is recommended for all ages from 5 and above. 

We understand that childcare can sometimes be a barrier for parents attending the theatre, so if you need to bring a child under the age of five, you should

  • Consider the suitability, content, length of performance (2 hours) and age recommendation.
  • Be mindful and respectful of other customers’ enjoyment of the event before attending with younger children.
  • Try to book a seat near an aisle/exit so you can leave should your child become restless.

All children over the age of 24 months must have their own ticket. Children under 24 months do not need a ticket and should be seated on an adult’s lap.

What is Planet Play?

A magical Friday morning for your littlest ones. 

Planet Play is a warm, sensory experience designed especially for babies and toddlers aged 0–3. 

Through soft sounds, gentle movement and immersive performance, we create a magical space where the youngest members of our community can explore, wonder and play. 

Grown-ups go free — just book a ticket for yourself and bring your little one along. The perfect weekly ritual or one-off treat.

About Tales from the Shed

Pull up a seat and get ready for some Tales magic. 

Tales from the Shed is Chickenshed's beloved Saturday morning show for babies, toddlers and young children. Each week, our brilliant performers bring a brand new story to life — full of music, movement, silliness and warmth. 

With two shows every Saturday (10am and 11:30am), it's the perfect start to the weekend for little ones and grown-ups alike. No experience needed — just come along, settle in and let the story begin.

Free to babies under 6mths

Educational Songs

Inclusive theatre shows

What is Tales from the Shed?

Each carefully crafted Tales from the Shed show is packed with educational songs, movement, and language games, designed to support brain development and early learning in young children. We celebrate diversity and inclusion in everything we do, creating a space where all children - no matter their background or ability can take part and feel the magic of theatre.

Every week brings a brand-new theme, making each performance a unique adventure! Having worked alongside early years experts for over three decades, our diverse team brings stories to life with much-loved characters like Can-Can the beautiful bird, laid-back Lion Down, and the hilarious Thing That Goes Blurgh! 

These stories aren't just entertaining - they're designed to inspire creativity, promote emotional expression, and foster social interaction among children.

At Tales from the Shed, we believe in the power of performance to spark joy, curiosity, and connection. By encouraging participation, we invite children to actively engage with the stories, helping to create lasting memories and nurturing a love for learning.

Age Restriction

Tales from the Shed is for children from 0-6 years only. With the exception of older siblings, no children over the age of 6 will be admitted.

If you wish to know more about why this is policy is being enforced please email Pete Dowse (peted@chickenshed.or.uk) or Loren Jacobs (lorenj@chickenshed.org.uk) from the Tales team

Seating

Seating is mostly on mats on the floor so that children and performers can freely move around the space. Chairs are available for anyone who would prefer not to sit on the floor

Pricing

You will need to purchase a ticket for everyone from the age of 6 months. If you are bringing a child under 6 months they are free of charge and you do not need to get them a ticket

Tales Birthday Parties

The perfect way to celebrate your little one's birthday!

Book a party today!

Accessibility

We've got you covered with baby changing, disabled access, space to park buggies and even a cafè to get a tasty treat!Limited free parking is available in front of the building.

If you have specific access requirements, feel free to contact us in advance so that we can make sure your needs are catered for.

What is Boots & Beats?

Saddle up — we're going dancing. 

Boots & Beats is our brand new fundraising evening and it promises to be one of the most fun nights of the year. Expert instructors from The Cactus Club (led by the brilliant Peter Flockhard) will guide you through a brilliant line dancing session — and you absolutely do not need experience to join in. The music spans far beyond country, so there's something for everyone. 

No dress code, but cowboy boots and hats are absolutely encouraged! This is an aerobic activity.

All proceeds support Chickenshed's work with children, young people and communities. 

Event information

Doors open at 6.30pm

We’ll open the doors before we get dancing so that everyone can arrive, grab a drink, and settle in before the dancing begins.

Dancing begins at 7pm!

It's time to hit the dance floor led by The Cactus Club who’ll guide you through a mix of easy-to-follow routines, perfect whether you’ve danced before or are trying it for the first time. Expect a lively mix of music across the night, not just country, but a wide range of feel-good tracks to keep everyone moving.

8pm - take a break to refuel

We’ll take a short break for some light refreshments to refuel and enjoy the atmosphere.

8.30pm - back in line!

Show off your new moves, put your new-found skills to the test and strut your stuff on the dance floor for more dancing, laughter and feel-good tunes, followed by the evening's raffle!

What to wear?

There's no set dress code though please make sure you're comfortable and ready to dance! Cowboy boots are very welcome (and highly encouraged for extra dance-floor flair), though this isn't specifically a country music night. Expect a fun mix of music, movement, community and laughter throughout the evening.
